messages:
alerts-bot: Paging: Dedicated pool eu-west-1 - hotshot priority queue p99 > 3s for 6+ minutes. SLO breach threshold exceeded. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west1/dedicated/pool/latency

sre_oncall: Oncall here. Confirming — p95 jumped from ~220ms to 1.1s, p99 ~4.5s. Streaming stalls observed (chat-stream).

taylor_j: seeing queue_depth spike on the pool controller: backlog ~11.8k, warmup backlog ~5.9k. Autoscaler logs show repeated handshake timeouts and delayed slot assignment.

priya: any recent rollout that touched pool sizing or handshake? I don't see infra deploys in the last 2h.

chen: no deploys. Autoscaler metrics show surge of hotshot requests from a single customer bucket (enterprise-omega) + multiple small bursts from PLG flows. Priority queue overwhelmed.

ops_prod: snippet from autoscaler logs 
```
[2025-07-21T03:25:44Z] scale_request(id=pool-eu-1) state=queued reason=warmup delay=0.6s
[2025-07-21T03:26:12Z] handshake=timeout pool_slot=-1 err=slot_alloc_fail
[2025-07-21T03:26:45Z] scale_request(id=pool-eu-1) state=delayed reason=handshake_backoff backoff=12s
```

product-support: Customer impact: enterprise-omega reported streaming stalls and several aborted sessions — support ticket #INC-4829, 8 customers affected, first seen ~03:22 UTC.

sre_oncall: Triage plan: 1) throttle non-enterprise priority flows (reduce hotshot quota for free_tier/beta) 2) force-spin additional reserved hotshot nodes (emergency override) 3) enable fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint for streaming (lower memory warmup) 4) if needed, move enterprise-omega to dedicated temp-capacity.

taylor_j: I've applied a soft throttle on free_tier via routing rules (priority_weight=0.3). Observing immediate minor relief in queue_depth (-18%).

chen: requesting ops_prod to run emergency spin-up: `rmqctl trigger-hotshot-override --region eu-west-1 --slots 6 --reason "pg-flood"` — this uses reserved burst capacity.

ops_prod: running now. ETA ~65s per slot to warm up (kv load + model init). Starting 6 slots.

alerts-bot: Action logged: emergency-burst-override invoked by ops_prod. Incident tag: #hotshot-flood-1739001111

priya: while warmup spins, we need short-term mitigation for streaming stalls: enable streaming fallback to stateless-rt variant (no KV) for sessions >60s. That will avoid warmup. Anyone object?

product-support: go for it — will notify affected customers that we're rerouting to low-latency variant to reduce stalls (may change cost/quality slightly).

taylor_j: streaming fallback enabled for tail sessions. Early telemetry: p99 reduced from 4.5s -> 2.1s on affected routes. Tail stalls reduced but backlog still present.

chen: new autoscaler logs show handshake success for the first two slots after ~72s. Queue_depth trending down from 11.8k -> 4.3k in 4 minutes.

sre_oncall: Good. Continuing to monitor. Next steps: 1) keep emergency slots until steady < 1k backlog + p99 < SLO 1s 2) follow up with rate-limit policy changes for priority queue to prevent single-customer flood 3) collect traces and add to postmortem.

priya: I'll open a short-term customer remediation playbook and notify account team about enterprise-omega remediation and credit.

product-support: noted. We've updated INC-4829 with mitigation steps and ETA for follow-up call.

alerts-bot: Recovery: p99 now 890ms, backlog 820. SLO restored at 03:52 UTC. Please update postmortem checklist.

sre_oncall: Marking incident as mitigated but not closed. Handing off to night oncall (taylor_j) for monitoring until 08:00 UTC. Primary action items: gather autoscaler handshake traces, evaluate hotshot reservation thresholds, and draft rate-limit rule for priority queue.

ops_prod: leaving emergency slots up for 30 more minutes then we'll drain.

product-support: prepping customer comms.

chen: putting initial notes into incident doc: https://docs.redwood/incidents/1739001111-hotshot-flood-triage.md

sre_oncall: Thanks team. We'll collect logs and reconvene if any regressions.
